entries.knownHazards: Although no specific mention of this plant as being toxic has been seen, it belongs to a family where there are some species that are said to be toxic. Caution should be observed. Any toxins are likely to be concentrated in the bulb[200].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Konkrečių toksiškumo duomenų nėra, tačiau šeimoje yra toksiškų rūšių — atsargumas patartinas. Toksinai labiausiai tikėtini svogūnėlyje.

entries.knownHazards: Skin contact with the bulb can cause dermatitis in sensitive people[65]. The bulb contains alkaloids and is poisonous[2, 62]. Another report says that the bulb is poisonous to grazing animals[183].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Svogūnėlis dirgina odą ir gali sukelti dermatitą jautriems žmonėms; jame esantys alkaloidai yra toksiški žmonėms ir ganomuosius gyvuliams.

entries.knownHazards: The plant is rich in calcium oxylate, this is toxic and if consumed makes the mouth and digestive tract feel as though hundreds of needles are being stuck into it. However, calcium oxylate is easily destroyed by thoroughly cooking or drying the plant.
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Augale gausu kalcio oksalatų, kurie dirgina burną ir virškinamąjį traktą. Kruopščiai kepant arba džiovinant jie suskyla ir pašalinamas pavojus.

entries.knownHazards: Although we have found no reports of toxicity for this species, a number of ferns contain carcinogens so some caution is advisable[200]. Many ferns also contain thiaminase, an enzyme that robs the body of its vitamin B complex. In small quantities this enzyme will do no harm to people eating an adequate diet that is rich in vitamin B, though large quantities can cause severe health problems. The enzyme is destroyed by heat or thorough drying, so cooking the plant will remove the thiaminase[172].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Paparčiai gali turėti kancerogeninių medžiagų ir tiaminazės fermento, kuris ardo B grupės vitaminus; didelės dozės kenksmingos. Terminis apdorojimas arba kruopštus džiovinimas tiaminazę sunaikina.

entries.knownHazards: The leaves contain oxalic acid, which gives them their sharp flavour. Perfectly all right in small quantities, the leaves should not be eaten in large amounts since oxalic acid can bind up the body's supply of calcium leading to nutritional deficiency. The quantity of oxalic acid will be reduced if the leaves are cooked. People with a tendency to rheumatism, arthritis, gout, kidney stones or hyperacidity should take especial caution if including this plant in their diet since it can aggravate their condition[238].
entries.knownHazardsLtV2: Lapuose yra oksalatų, kurie dideliais kiekiais mažina organizmo kalcio atsargas; virimas sumažina jų kiekį. Sergantieji reumatu, podagra, inkstų akmenimis ar hiperacidumu turėtų vengti šio augalo.

entries.knownHazards: This plant contains a number of very toxic compounds, many of which are extracted and used as pain killers etc in medicine. They are also used to make various highly addictive narcotic drugs[7, 10, 19, 65]. However, in the cooler climate of Britain these compounds are not formed in sufficient quantity to make their extraction worthwhile. There are no toxins in the seeds[10, 46, 65].
